problem.text: Let $n$ be a positive integer and $d$ be a digit such that the value of the numeral $\underline{32d}$ in base $n$ equals $263$, and the value of the numeral $\underline{324}$ in base $n$ equals the value of the numeral $\underline{11d1}$ in base six. What is $n + d$?

steps.title: Where to start: turn every numeral into base ten
steps.body:
Numerals in unknown bases are hard to compare, but in base ten they become ordinary algebra. In base $n$ the digits of a three-digit numeral stand for $n^2$, $n$ and $1$, so the first fact becomes
$$\underline{32d}_n = 3n^2 + 2n + d = 263.$$

your_turn.prompt: Write $\underline{11d1}$ in base six as a base-ten expression in $d$.

steps.title: Two equations, one shared piece
steps.body: The second fact says $\underline{324}_n = \underline{11d1}_6$, which is $3n^2 + 2n + 4 = 253 + 6d$. Both equations contain $3n^2 + 2n$, and the first one tells us $3n^2 + 2n = 263 - d$. Substitute that into the second equation to get rid of $n$.

steps.title: Put it together
steps.body: With $d = 2$ the first equation is $3n^2 + 2n + 2 = 263$, so $3n^2 + 2n - 261 = 0$, which factors as $(3n + 29)(n - 9) = 0$. Since $n$ is positive, $n = 9$ (and base $9$ is big enough for the digits $3, 2, 4$). Check: $\underline{322}_9 = 243 + 18 + 2 = 263$. So $n + d = 9 + 2 = 11$. The answer is **(B)** $11$.
